name: docs_portal
note: Long goal: a documentation portal that stops going stale. Two milestones, a simple linear dependency — the smallest honest DAG, and the fixture that proves a short plan is not a degraded one.

mission.goal: Our documentation portal drifts out of date within weeks of every release, and support keeps answering questions the docs already claim to cover. The pages themselves are not bad; the problem is that nothing connects a shipped change to the page that describes it, so nobody notices when a page becomes a lie. What we want, eventually, is a portal where a stale page is detected by the build rather than by an annoyed customer, and where the person shipping a change is told which pages their change makes wrong. Rewriting the portal's design or changing the static site generator is explicitly not wanted.

milestones.goal: every documentation page is linked to the code it describes
milestones.rationale: Staleness cannot be detected before the link between page and code exists.

jobs_draft.title: Introduce a page-to-source reference
jobs_draft.goal: Each page declares the modules or endpoints it documents

jobs_draft.title: Backfill references for the existing pages
jobs_draft.goal: Every current page carries a reference or an explicit none

milestones.goal: the build fails on a page the code has outgrown
milestones.rationale: A check a human has to remember to run is a check that does not exist.

jobs_draft.title: Add the staleness gate to the docs build
jobs_draft.goal: A referenced symbol that moved or vanished fails the build

risks: Pages that document behaviour rather than a symbol may have no natural reference.
assumptions: The static site generator and the portal design stay as they are.
